Built for productivity."), product demo animation, customer logos, product modules (Channels / Huddles / Canvas / Workflow / AI), customer stories | | `pricing.html` | Pricing: four columns Free / Pro / Business+ / Enterprise+, yearly / monthly toggle, feature comparison table (message history, Slack Connect, Workflow Builder, AI, Support, etc.), FAQ | | `features.html` | Feature detail page: modules for Channels / Canvas / Clips / Huddles / Workflows / AI |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full slack system, prioritizing the primary pricing flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The evaluation covered the Slack marketing clone, focusing on the pricing, contact, and account creation flows across desktop and mobile. While dynamic pricing updates and form success states function smoothly, severe usability issues exist on mobile, including a highly cramped header that causes text collision and undersized tap targets like a 13x13px consent checkbox. Desktop flows are hampered by non-functional SSO buttons, broken anchor links, and missing icon assets. Note that only 16% of visible interactive features were directly exercised, leaving many deep interactions untested.

exploration_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore and evaluate the UX of the Slack clone, focusing on the pricing flow, authentication/lead forms, and informational pages across desktop and mobile viewports.
exploration_plan.summary: Begin by validating core navigation and homepage elements. Proceed to a deep dive into the pricing page to test interactive toggles and plan comparisons. Next, evaluate the contact, sign-in, and get-started forms for usability and validation states. Finally, review deep content pages (Features, Enterprise, etc.) and repeat critical checks on a mobile viewport to assess responsive design and small tap target issues.
assumptions: The pricing page contains a functional monthly/annual toggle that updates prices dynamically.
Form submissions (Contact Sales, Sign In) will rely on frontend validation rather than a real backend.
Navigation links reported as 'small tap targets' might be hidden behind a hamburger menu on mobile.
risk_hotspots: pricing.html: Monthly/Annual toggle functionality and visual clarity
contact.html: Form validation and error messaging for required fields
Global Navigation: Numerous 'small tap target' warnings suggest potential usability issues on touch devices
features.html: Anchor links jumping to specific sections (e.g., #channels, #ai)

phases.title: Homepage & Core Navigation
phases.objective: Verify the homepage renders correctly and core navigation links successfully route to primary sections.
key_checks: Click primary navigation links (Features, Solutions, Enterprise, Pricing)
Verify CTA buttons ('Get started free', 'Talk to sales')
exit_criteria: Successfully navigated to at least 3 distinct top-level pages from the homepage.

phases.title: Pricing Deep Dive
phases.objective: Thoroughly test the pricing page interactions, particularly the billing toggle and plan structure.
key_checks: Interact with the 'Monthly / Annual' billing toggle and observe price changes
exit_criteria: Billing toggle state change is verified and all plan tiers are reviewed.

phases.title: Forms & Authentication flows
phases.objective: Evaluate input fields, form validation, and layout of lead generation and auth pages.
key_checks: Attempt to submit the 'Talk to sales' form empty to trigger validation errors
Fill out required fields (Name, Email, Company Size, etc.) in contact.html
Interact with 'Continue with...' SSO buttons and standard login fields on auth pages
exit_criteria: Contact form validation is tested and auth page layouts are verified.

phases.title: Deep Content & Anchor Links
phases.objective: Ensure informational pages present content clearly and in-page navigation works.
key_checks: Review layout and typography of text-heavy pages like Trust & Security or About
exit_criteria: All secondary informational pages are visited and scrolled.

phases.title: Mobile Responsiveness
phases.objective: Re-evaluate critical UI components on a mobile viewport, focusing on reported tap target warnings.
key_checks: Open and use the mobile navigation menu
Verify the pricing table is readable and scrollable on small screens
Ensure form inputs on contact.html are usable on touch
exit_criteria: Mobile navigation and primary pricing/form interactions are successfully executed in mobile mode.

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all 11 HTML pages identified in the prescan.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise the pricing toggle, submit the contact form, and test at least one anchor link.
coverage_targets.mobile: Test global navigation, pricing page, and contact form in the mobile viewport.

notes: Pay special attention to the layout warnings regarding small tap targets in the global header; these must be flagged if they persist on mobile without a proper hamburger menu.

findings.user_goal: Sign into the application or access main navigation on a mobile device.
findings.problem: The mobile header is severely cramped, with zero margin between the Slack logo and the 'Sign in' link, causing the 'Sign in' text to wrap awkwardly and creating a high risk of accidental misclicks.
findings.evidence: In the mobile viewport on index.html, the 'Sign in' link has a tap target width of just 34px and is stacked vertically ('Sign' over 'in') immediately adjacent to the logo.
findings.why_it_matters: A cluttered and malformed primary navigation bar severely degrades the first impression on mobile, making it difficult for returning users to find and tap the login button.
findings.suggestion: Increase the spacing between header elements, ensure 'Sign in' displays on a single line (or use an icon), and increase its tap target area to at least 44x44px.

findings.user_goal: Opt into communications when submitting the Contact Sales form on a mobile device.
findings.problem: The consent checkbox on the mobile Contact Sales form is extremely small, making it difficult to accurately tap with a finger.
findings.evidence: Observation during steps 73-78 on the mobile contact.html page revealed the checkbox dimensions are 13x13px, well below the standard 44px mobile guidance.
findings.why_it_matters: Extremely small tap targets on mobile devices lead to accidental misclicks, user frustration, and friction in completing critical lead generation forms.
findings.suggestion: Increase the sizing of the custom checkbox or add adequate padding to the input and its associated `<label>` to ensure the combined clickable area is at least 44x44px.

findings.user_goal: Quickly create a new account using Google Single Sign-On.
findings.problem: The 'Continue with Google' SSO button on the Get Started page is completely non-functional and provides no feedback when clicked.
findings.evidence: During steps 37-42, clicking the 'Continue with Google' button on get-started.html resulted in no page transition, error message, or visual state change.
findings.why_it_matters: Users expect SSO to be the fastest and easiest way to sign up. A broken SSO button blocks this preferred path, causing abandonment and damaging trust during onboarding.
findings.suggestion: Implement the SSO authentication flow or temporarily hide the button if the integration is not yet active. Ensure visual feedback (like a loading spinner) is shown immediately upon click.

findings.user_goal: Correctly fill out and submit lead generation and signup forms.
findings.problem: Submitting empty required forms relies entirely on native HTML5 browser tooltips for a single field at a time, failing to provide comprehensive inline validation.
findings.evidence: Tested in steps 07-12; submitting the empty Contact Sales form triggers a native browser popup on the first invalid field, but lacks inline textual error messages for all missing fields simultaneously.
findings.why_it_matters: Native browser validation is often inconsistent across browsers and devices, forcing the user to fix errors one-by-one rather than seeing a holistic view of what needs correction.
findings.suggestion: Implement custom JavaScript validation to display clear, red inline error messages below all invalid fields simultaneously upon form submission, while preventing the default HTML5 popups.

findings.user_goal: Find and apply for open job positions at the company.
findings.problem: The 'View open positions' call-to-action on the About Us page misleadingly redirects users to the generic account creation page.
findings.evidence: In steps 49-54, clicking 'View open positions' on about.html navigated directly to get-started.html instead of a careers page.
findings.why_it_matters: Misleading links break user expectations, causing confusion and frustration for prospective applicants trying to navigate the site for company information.
findings.suggestion: Update the href attribute to point to a dedicated careers page or an external applicant tracking system (ATS) portal.

findings.user_goal: Browse available resources and help documentation easily.
findings.problem: The Resources page fails to render icons for its list items, displaying raw fallback text characters instead of proper visual glyphs.
findings.evidence: Observed in steps 19-24 and 55-60 on resources.html; list items like 'Help Centre' and 'What's New' are preceded by unstyled characters like '?', 'N', and '</>'.
findings.why_it_matters: Broken assets make the site look unprofessional and unfinished, which degrades brand trust and reduces the scannability of the resource links.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the icon font library (e.g., FontAwesome, Material Icons) or SVG assets are correctly imported, referenced in the CSS, and not blocked by CORS policies.

findings.user_goal: Filter the feature comparison table on the Pricing page while scrolling.
findings.problem: The sticky global navigation header overlaps and partially obscures the feature comparison table's filter buttons when they approach the top of the viewport.
findings.evidence: Recorded in steps 01-06 on pricing.html: 'The sticky site header overlaps and partially obscures the feature comparison filter buttons... which impairs readability and clickability.'
findings.why_it_matters: If filter buttons are hidden beneath the header, users cannot change their view of the comparison table while scrolling, reducing the utility of the table.
findings.suggestion: Apply a `scroll-margin-top` to the filter section or implement a secondary sticky header for the filters that rests directly below the primary global header.

findings.user_goal: Jump directly to the AI features section using the secondary navigation.
findings.problem: The 'Intelligence' anchor link in the secondary navigation on the Features page does not function, resulting in no page movement.
findings.evidence: Tested in steps 61-66: 'The Intelligence anchor link (href="#ai") does not function. Clicking it results in no page scroll or visible text change.'
findings.why_it_matters: Broken in-page navigation prevents users from quickly finding the specific content they are interested in, leading to higher bounce rates on long-form content pages.
findings.suggestion: Verify that a target element with the `id="ai"` exists on the page and that no JavaScript is intercepting and incorrectly preventing default anchor scrolling behavior.

gaps: Only directly exercised 16% of visible interactive feature signatures.
